feed.title: [BIP draft] Unspendable Internal Keys for Wallet Policies

entry.title: [BIP draft] Unspendable Internal Keys for Wallet Policies
entry.summary:
The ongoing efforts to standardize an unspendable NUMS key for a script path only in the taproot policy have been detailed in recent discussions and proposals. Key points include the decision not to enforce adherence to other Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) unless they directly impact the matter at hand. Existing mechanisms established by previous BIPs are utilized, avoiding the assertion of semantic canonicalization of the script while normalizing the policy to a certain opinionated extent.
In terms of technical specifics, a placeholder symbol '_' has been designated for the unspendable NUMS key within the script. This approach involves sorting keys within the 'musig(..)' function and 'sortedmulti_a' identifier, as well as ordering sibling pairs in the tree structure. To address potential issues with multipath extensions, an equal length tuple is added to the placeholder to prevent key reuse. Subsequently, keys are extracted using '@i' placeholders, and the entire assembly comprising the normalized descriptor and keys is hashed. This hash serves as the chain code for the H defined in BIP 341.
Further details and the full proposal can be reviewed on the GitHub repository under the discussion [Unspendable Keys in Descriptors](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/unspendable-keys-in-descriptors/304) and the pull request [Bitcoin BIPs Pull #1746](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/1746). Additionally, comprehensive information regarding these implementations can be found in the Mediawiki document at [BIP-XXXX Unspendable Internal Keys](https://github.com/bitryonix/bips/blob/bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys/bip-xxxx-unspendable-internal-keys.mediawiki).
